summary: Customer (NovaHealth) reviewed Redwood's data residency and region-pinning capabilities. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (NovaHealth CISO), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform), Emily Zhang (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Sofia Martinez: hi, sofia here, CISO at NovaHealth. main reason we're on is to validate data residency and region pinning — we have strict EU residency reqs for patient metadata and some logs.
[00:20] Jordan Hayes: got it. priya and i will walk through how redwood handles region pinning, routing fallback and subprocessor relationships.
[00:28] Priya Nair: hi all, priya, i'm the SE. i'll focus on the technical flow — where data lives, how we pin requests to regions, and the encryption/KMS options.
[00:36] Liam O'Connor: timeline note — we're aiming for a pilot in q3, decision by end of quarter if the tech + compliance fit.
[00:44] Emily Zhang: legal will need the sub-processor list and any cross-border transfer details, plus sample contract language about processing locations.

[01:02] Priya Nair: quick overview — Redwood supports region pinning at the route level. you can pin a route to EU or US; that sets compute + short-lived storage for inference to the selected region. for hosted customers we also offer private deployments (VPC) for additional separation.
[01:18] Sofia Martinez: when you say short-lived storage, does that include logs and kv cache? we need metadata and outputs to never leave EU for pinned routes.
[01:28] Priya Nair: good question — main request payload and generated outputs for a pinned route stay in the pin region by default. KV cache and prefix caching can be configured to be regional. however there are some control-plane operations that are global — meta telemetry is anonymized and we can control what leaves region. we also offer options for customer-managed KMS so keys for encryption at rest can be EU-located.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: clarification — what about model artifacts and fallbacks? if EU capacity is constrained, do you route to US? that's a dealbreaker.
[01:56] Jordan Hayes: we have routing policies — by default, pinned routes will only use capacity in the pinned region. fallback to other regions is configurable and off by default for compliance-sensitive customers. you can set strict pinning: no cross-border serving.
[02:12] Emily Zhang: what about sub-processors — who has access to the data (even transiently)? cloud providers, monitoring, telemetry, etc.
[02:20] Priya Nair: sub-processor list — primary infra is AWS in eu-west and us-west regions, also GCP for some customers, and a CDN provider for some static assets. we maintain a sub-processor register and will share it; for private deployments you can avoid certain public sub-processors.
[02:36] Sofia Martinez: do you have any EU-only sub-processors or subcontractors? any us-based engineering team accessing logs?
[02:44] Jordan Hayes: support and engineering access are role-based — no direct engineer access to customer data in pinned routes unless there's an approved IR and scope. audit logs capture access events. we can provide an org-level RBAC export and show how SSO/SAML maps to roles.

[03:10] Priya Nair: encryption — at rest we support AES-256 and customer-managed keys via KMS. customers can bring keys in AWS KMS (eu-west) or use HSM integrations for higher assurance. in transit is TLS 1.2+; we also support mutual TLS for private endpoints.
[03:30] Liam O'Connor: can you support a model where the inference happens in EU but logs or billing metadata goes to US? that's a subtlety — our auditors treat metadata differently depending on content.
[03:40] Priya Nair: right — we classify telemetry: PII-bearing outputs vs operational metrics. operational metrics (latency, token counts) can be aggregated and anonymized and sent to centralized analytics in another region; anything considered content or identifiers can be configured to stay in-region. we'll work with your compliance team to map fields.
[03:58] Emily Zhang: retention windows — our policy requires audit logs retained for 7 years for certain data. can Redwood support long-term retention in EU for audit logs?
[04:06] Jordan Hayes: yes, we can configure retention windows. longer retention may move logs to cost-effective storage tiers but we can keep them in-region. we'll need to review retention SLA and pricing implications.

[04:28] Sofia Martinez: about cross-border subprocessors — do you use any us-based analytics or third-party monitoring that might touch logs?
[04:36] Priya Nair: we use some hosted monitoring and alerting — most customers with strict residency either opt for private deployment or we configure monitoring to redact content and keep the log blobs in-region. we'll include the sub-processor matrix with levels of access.

[05:00] Liam O'Connor: curious about the control plane — are customer names or route metadata stored globally? our lawyers flagged global metadata as a risk if it can identify EU customers.
[05:10] Priya Nair: control plane metadata (route names, config) is stored in the control plane which can be hosted in a customer's region for private customers; for hosted we can limit what metadata is replicated and anonymize identifiers. we'll provide the control-plane diagram.

[05:28] Jordan Hayes: for SOC2/ISO — we will send the latest SOC2 report and ISO27001 cert. we also have penetration test summaries and an SSAE-type attestation.
[05:38] Emily Zhang: perfect — legal will review, but we usually need the actual reports and AICPA letter.

[05:46] Priya Nair: SSO/RBAC — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC for SSO. RBAC maps to roles like admin/developer/audit. you can restrict support access to read-only for audit logs. we also support audit log streaming to your SIEM (via syslog or S3 ingestion) in-region.
[06:10] Sofia Martinez: SIEM ingestion — can you push to an EU S3 bucket? and can keys be customer-managed?
[06:18] Priya Nair: yes to both. we can push logs to customer-owned EU S3 with server-side encryption using your keys, or we can encrypt and send to an endpoint you control.

[06:36] Liam O'Connor: about the fallback behavior again — show us a config snippet that enforces strict pinning.
[06:44] Priya Nair: i'll include a config example in the follow-up note: route.pinning = "eu-west-1"; fallback = false; allowed_subprocessors = [list]; kms_location = "eu-west-1". note: in hosted mode, there are operational limits, we'll discuss capacity planning for reserved/dedicated pools.

[07:08] Jordan Hayes: quick run of typical Q&A we see — customers ask about cross-border backups, support access, key escrow, and sub-processor termination clauses. most are handled via private deployment or contractual terms.
[07:24] Emily Zhang: can we get a redwood-hosted contract sample with EU data processing addendum?
[07:30] Jordan Hayes: yes, we'll include a DPA and sample contract language.

[07:40] Sofia Martinez: any latency implications for strict EU pinning if we choose a smaller dedicated pool? some of our traffic is real-time and latency sensitive.
[07:50] Priya Nair: latency depends on model choice and batch sizes; dedicated pools in eu-west with appropriate GPU class will meet low-latency SLOs. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching to reduce cost without harming latency. we'll include perf numbers from similar customers.

[08:10] Liam O'Connor: can we run a short PoC that validates: 1) EU-only serving (no cross-border), 2) audit log capture and delivery to our EU S3, 3) KMS keys in our AWS account? timeline ~2 weeks?
[08:20] Jordan Hayes: yes, that's reasonable. we'll scope the PoC and get it scheduled.

[08:28] Priya Nair: one more note on sub-processors — we use a small set of third parties; we'll provide the register and highlight which ones touch content vs just infra metadata.

[08:40] Emily Zhang: ok thanks, that helps. we'll expect the certs and sub-processor list and then schedule a follow-up with security and legal.

[08:50] Jordan Hayes: recap / next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO, sub-processor register, region-pinning tech note with config snippet, sample DPA, and propose PoC dates. priya will include an architecture diagram and config snippet.
[09:04] Sofia Martinez: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:08] Jordan Hayes: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.
